cd4ef6f98f.q: Why did Jo Calver split Isla James Interiors and Isla James Lighting into two separate companies?
cd4ef6f98f.a: Jo wanted the lighting division to operate independently so other interior designers and architects could approach them without conflict of interest, since the services were previously integrated. She also recognized that international clients perceive London as the design hub, making a London-based address critical for the lighting business to compete globally, whereas the interior design studio could operate successfully from Berkshire.

e2dd6526ca.q: What was Jo Calver's approach to hiring her first employee and what did she recommend about experience level?
e2dd6526ca.a: Jo saved a full year's salary before taking on her first hire to feel secure about the commitment. She hired Sophie, a mid-weight designer with six and a half years of experience, rather than a junior, because experienced hires add immediate value, hit the ground running, and earn their salary in month one—avoiding the years of training and risk that come with junior staff.

2781bc7b1f.q: How does Jo Calver organize her interior design team into pods and manage project capacity?
2781bc7b1f.a: Jo organizes her 11-person team into three pods, each consisting of a senior designer, a mid-weight, and a junior designer assigned to roughly three major projects. She uses CMAP, an architectural project management system, to track all staff availability, holidays, invoicing, and time allocation across projects, allowing her to see exactly who can take on new work at any moment.

72a930d365.q: What was Jo Calver's experience transitioning from the NHS to entrepreneurship and what triggered her departure?
72a930d365.a: Jo worked as a paediatric nurse at John Radcliffe Hospital in Oxford for three months in the trauma unit and enjoyed the work but not the NHS culture. She left after being told she had to bring her own pen to work, which she felt symbolized a lack of care for staff. She then spent four years in pharmaceutical sales before eventually starting Isla James Interiors in 2015.
